label: Next-item ranking from sessions
summary: A runnable reference for recommending the next item from the current session: bot filtering, popularity, bag co-visitation, ordered transitions and a theme-aware model, evaluated by hit rate, MRR and coverage on a time split.
runtime: Python 3.11+ with numpy, pandas, scipy and pytest (about 25 seconds per run; the tests take about 30 seconds)
run: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
expected: make_data.py prints 60,000 sessions, about 360,000 clicks and 10% bot sessions. baseline.py reports HitRate@20 of 0.076 for popularity, 0.557 for bag co-visitation, 0.588 for ordered transitions and 0.597 for the theme-aware model (MRR 0.025, 0.224, 0.315 and 0.327). Leaving bots in training drops the theme-aware MRR to 0.273. pytest reports 8 passed.

files.purpose: Synthetic sessions with asymmetric item flow, themes, a sale and crawler bots
Time split, bot filter, four recommenders, leave-last-out evaluation and the two trap experiments
Executable gates for determinism, split, bot filter, evaluation protocol, model ordering and both traps

synthetic.description: 60,000 sessions (about 360,000 clicks) over 30 days on a 1,500-item catalogue with asymmetric item-to-item flow, a theme per session, a sale from day 22 and 10% crawler sessions that walk the catalogue in id order.
knobs: n_sessions, n_items, days: scale of the log
seed: identical seed gives an identical log

slots.meaning: the item the user is looking at now
the last few items in the session, in order
share of recent items in each category
recent interaction counts, corrected for popularity
time per item and traversal pattern used to remove non-human sessions

data.threshold: pytest -k 'deterministic or time_split or never_credits' passes: 0 sessions shared between train and test, with a gap day between them
data.how: Run pytest in the kit directory

features.threshold: At least 95% of crawler sessions removed and at least 98% of human sessions kept

baseline.threshold: Ordered transitions beat bag co-visitation on MRR by at least 0.04, and co-visitation reaches five times popularity's hit rate (the kit: MRR 0.315 against 0.224)

challenger.metric: No regression and a measured trap cost
challenger.threshold: Challenger within 0.005 of the ordered model on HitRate@20 and MRR@20, coverage above 50%, and bots in training cutting MRR by more than 10% (the kit: 0.597 and 0.327, and a 16% loss)

tests.pass: Training ends before the test window and no session id is on both sides
At least 95% of crawler sessions removed and 98% of humans kept
A recommender that echoes the last item scores a hit rate of 0
Ordered MRR exceeds bag MRR by 0.04 and co-visitation reaches five times popularity's hit rate
MRR with bots left in training is below 90% of MRR with the filter
Popularity hit rate on a random split exceeds the time-split figure by more than 10%

lessons.trap: Counting every click as a human signal
lessons.evidence: About 4,200 crawler sessions create a spurious transition for every item that outranks the real top successor; leaving them in training cuts MRR from 0.327 to 0.273.

lessons.trap: Treating the session as a bag of items
lessons.evidence: Ignoring click order scores MRR 0.224 against 0.315 when order is honoured.
A random split gives popularity a hit rate of 0.096 against 0.076 on a time split because a sale's popularity shift sits on both sides.

lessons.trap: Choosing a heavy model before measuring headroom
lessons.evidence: The theme-aware model adds only about one point of hit rate over plain ordered transitions.

target: There is no separate label: for each test session the prefix of clicks is the input and the final click is the target (leave-last-out). Sessions shorter than three clicks are skipped.

headline.baseline: HitRate@20 0.588 and MRR 0.315 for ordered transitions
